sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A clustering palm of Southeast Asian peat swamps. Its underground stems produce spiny pinnate leaves; the stems can reach about 8 m.

sections.title: Fruit and uses
sections.text: The scaly fruits are about 2–4 cm long and have very sour flesh. They are eaten fresh or fermented in some regions; young fronds are also reported as local food.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Documented uses concern locally prepared fruit and young fronds; they do not apply to other parts of the palm.
